2025_120_tsd_peps_report_march_2025.paragraph: Carried on the Troy School District Board of Education agenda for the meeting of April 1, 2025, this PDF is titled "TSD PEPS Report - March 2025" and is the district's PEPS (Pupil Enrollment Projection Study) report. The most consequential fact about the copy supplied for summarization is that its text layer did not extract as text: every page came through as raw font glyph-index codes - slash-delimited integer sequences - rather than characters, so no narrative sentence, table value, projection, or enrollment figure is recoverable from the source provided.
2025_120_tsd_peps_report_march_2025.page:
**Identification**
- Title: TSD PEPS Report - March 2025
- Board meeting date: April 1, 2025
- Format: PDF
- Subject: the district's PEPS report, i.e. its pupil enrollment projection study

**Extraction status**
The PDF's embedded fonts are subset fonts with no usable character mapping, so the text extraction produced glyph indices instead of letters and digits. Each line of the supplied source appears as a run of slash-delimited numbers with a repeating token standing in for the space character. The numbering restarts and is reassigned from one embedded font to the next, so the same index refers to different characters on different pages.

**What can be stated**
The file is long and page-structured, with a running header repeated at the top of many pages and with the bulk of the body consisting of dense tabular material - long rows of uniform-width numeric tokens, consistent with enrollment counts, grade-level breakdowns, and multi-year projection grids - interspersed with shorter caption and section-label lines and with graphic-heavy pages carrying little text. Section-heading structure and district map or figure pages are discernible from the layout alone.

**Caveat**
No figure from this report is reproduced here. Any enrollment count, birth count, projection year, grade cohort, building name, or percentage that a reader might expect from a pupil enrollment projection study is present in the original PDF but absent from the extracted text, and none has been inferred or supplied from other sources. A summary with substantive content will require re-extracting this PDF with optical character recognition or with a glyph-mapping decoder rather than the standard text layer.
2025_120_tsd_peps_report_march_2025.verbose:
Agenda item for the Troy School District Board of Education meeting of April 1, 2025, filed under the title "TSD PEPS Report - March 2025" and attached as a PDF. PEPS is the district's pupil enrollment projection study, the periodic demographic and enrollment forecast used to inform capacity, staffing, boundary, and facilities planning.

The controlling fact for this summary is a technical one. The PDF supplied for re-summarization does not carry a readable text layer. Its embedded fonts are subsetted without a ToUnicode mapping, and the extraction step therefore emitted raw glyph indices rather than characters. Every content line in the source arrives as a run of slash-delimited integers, with a single repeated token occupying the position of each space. The index-to-character assignment is local to each embedded font subset and is reassigned as new fonts are introduced, so the mapping changes from page to page and even between typefaces on the same page. Nothing in the extracted stream is legible as English text or as Arabic numerals.

Consequently no substantive content of the report is transcribed here. That includes, and is not limited to: total district enrollment, enrollment by building, enrollment by grade, kindergarten entry counts, resident live-birth counts, cohort-survival ratios, housing or development counts, Schools of Choice or non-resident counts, capacity or utilization figures, and every projected year in the forecast horizon. None of these were legible, none have been carried over from any other Troy School District document, and none have been reconstructed by inference. Writing any such figure would be fabrication rather than summarization, which is precisely the failure mode this re-summarization effort exists to eliminate.

What the source does permit is a description of the document's physical shape. It is a multi-page, page-formatted report. A short running header line repeats at the top of the majority of pages, and a second, shorter line beneath it varies from page to page in the manner of a section or figure label. The body is dominated by tabular material: long lines composed of many uniform-length numeric tokens arranged in regular columns, with left-hand label tokens of consistent length, which is the signature of grade-by-year or building-by-year projection grids. Several pages consist of only a handful of short lines, consistent with map, chart, or full-page graphic content whose labels sit outside the text layer. Other pages carry short stacked single-token lines of the sort used for chart axis tick labels and legends. Toward the end of the file the density of numeric tokens falls and short label-style lines predominate, consistent with summary or methodology pages.

For downstream use, this item should be treated as an unindexed attachment. Full-text search against it will return nothing, and the tiered summaries stored for it should not be relied on for any enrollment number. Recovering the content requires re-processing the original PDF - either by rendering the pages and running optical character recognition, or by reconstructing the per-font glyph-index tables and decoding the existing stream. Until one of those is done, the record for this document is limited to its title, its format, its identification as the district's pupil enrollment projection study report for March 2025, and its placement on the April 1, 2025 Board of Education agenda.

2025_121_m022525bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of February 25, 2025, held at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, called to order by President Philippart at 7:00 p.m. and adjourned at 8:55 p.m. with all seven members present. The Board approved a six-item consent agenda and awarded five capital purchases, the largest being the Athletics Phase 2 high school renovation bid package totaling $12,895,203.00 against the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. It also adopted a resolution urging Congress to pass the IDEA Full Funding Act (S.2217/H.R. 4519).
2025_121_m022525bdmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Board of Education, Troy, Michigan. Board Meeting minutes, February 25, 2025, Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.; also present were Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler, Superintendent Machesky, and administrators Montante, Griffor, Griffin, Jansen, and Trudel, with approximately 75 members of the audience. Adjourned at 8:55 p.m. Submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary.

**Recognitions**
- All-State Athletes Fall 2024, presented by Athletic Director Matt Jansen: sixteen students across boys' soccer, boys' tennis, and boys' and girls' cross country, plus coaches Adam Spinks, Kevin McConnell, Mike Messina, Andrew Shipp, and Brian Miska.
- Mission Moment - IA-East capstone: Thyra Foronda, International Academy East sophomore, for her IB Middle Years Programme Personal Project and her nonprofit YPLA (Youth Peace & Language Association).
- Mission Moment - SSAB Executive Committee: leaders of the 56-member Superintendent Student Advisory Board, who ran the MLK Citywide Celebration and Day of Service.
- Student Spotlight: Nurayda Albeez of the TSD Creative Guild, introduced by advisor Thomas Butcher.

**Consent agenda** (Haupt/Anne; Yes 7, No 0)
Items A-F: January 14, 2025 Workshop minutes; January 21, 2025 Organizational & Regular Meeting minutes; Treasurer's Report - December 2024; Schools Closed to Open Enrollment; Schools of Choice 105 & 105c; Secondary Course Description Book Adoption. Personnel and Curriculum: none.

**Business - Athletics Phase 2** (Anne/Alic; Yes 7, No 0), 2023 Capital Projects Fund

| Contractor | Scope | Amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cortis Bros Trucking & Excavating | Site Work | $8,315,200.00 |
| E&L Construction Group | General Trades | 1,414,000.00 |
| Great Lakes Hotel Supply | Food Service Equipment | 80,766.00 |
| CSM Mechanical | Mechanical | 348,185.00 |
| Innovated Energy Controls | Electrical | 803,307.00 |
| Shaw Integrated & Turf Solutions, Inc. | Synthetic Turf | 978,545.00 |
| Contingency (8%) | | $955,200.00 |
| TOTAL | | $12,895,203.00 |

**Other business awards**
- Moving services (Melton/Haupt; Yes 7, No 0): Premier Relocations, LLC, $246,180.00, Capital Projects Fund.
- Network and wireless project (Haupt/Anne): Cisco Networks solution purchased through People Driven Technology, $2,154,355.01, 2023 Capital Projects Fund; Mr. Trudel said the district would be eligible for E-rate funding after April 1st. No vote tally is printed for this item.
- EPIC PA, bell, and security system (Alic/Haupt; Yes 7, No 0): VSC, Inc., $1,826,553.30, 2023 Capital Projects Fund.
- Martell cafeteria tables (Zendler/Anne; Yes 7, No 0): School Specialty, $39,786.15, Capital Projects Fund.

**Other actions**
- IDEA Full Funding Act resolution (Melton/Alic; Yes 7, No 0), calling on Congress to pass S.2217/H.R. 4519. Cited: Congress has never funded IDEA higher than 18%, funding dropped to 10.3% this year at a cost to Michigan of roughly $650 million; the 1975 federal commitment was 40 percent of average per pupil expenditure; current funding is approximately 10.7 percent; 10.69 percent of Troy students have disabilities.
- MASB Board of Directors' election (Anne/Haupt; Yes 7, No 0): ballot cast for Randel Meisner, Region 8, three-year term.

**Public communication and reports**
No speakers on agenda items; four community members spoke on non-agenda items with no action taken. Student representatives Kristian Vitanovich (TCCHS), Nurayda Albeez (IA-East), and Diana D'Aloisio (Athens) reported; Adam McManus (Troy High) was absent. Announcements included Schools of Choice addition of 70 students, AARC meetings, and the March 4, March 8, and March 18 Board dates.
2025_121_m022525bdmtg.verbose:
Minutes of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, for the Board Meeting of February 25, 2025, held at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Dr. Philippart, present were Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, Griffor, Griffin, Jansen, and Trudel. There were approximately 75 members of the audience. The minutes close "Respectfully submitted, Emina Alic, Secretary, Troy Board of Education," with the notation EA/jh.

RECOGNITION - ALL-STATE ATHLETES FALL 2024. Mr. Matt Jansen, Director of Athletics, recognized students named All-State Athletes in their respective sports: Graham Bauman (Boys' Soccer, 2nd Team), Marc Delikat (Boys' Soccer, 3rd Team), Dhruv Gupta (Boys' Tennis, 1st Team), Audrey Hamilton (Girls' Cross Country), Jesse Hao (Boys' Tennis, 1st Team), Prabath Inturi (Boys' Tennis, 1st Team), Daniel Kadiu (Boys' Soccer, 1st Team), Nick Kamugunga (Boys' Soccer, 3rd Team), Derrick Kim (Boys' Tennis, 1st Team), Nahuel Larroquette (Boys' Soccer, 2nd Team), Madie Miller (Girls' Cross Country), Neel Nagappala (Boys' Tennis, 1st Team), Ishan Patel (Boys' Tennis, 1st Team), Kian Schneeweis (Boys' Cross Country), Varun Shetty (Boys' Tennis, 1st Team), and Anthony Wu (Boys' Tennis, 1st Team). Coaches Adam Spinks, Kevin McConnell, Mike Messina, Andrew Shipp, and Brian Miska were also recognized. The students came up to receive a certificate and congratulations from the Board.

TSD MISSION MOMENT - IA-EAST CAPSTONE EXPERIENCE, IB MIDDLE YEARS PROGRAMME. The Board recognized Thyra Foronda, a sophomore at the International Academy East, for excellence in her MYP Personal Project, the capstone experience of the IB Middle Years Programme, in which all sophomores spend a semester investigating a topic of their choice. Foronda is the founder of YPLA (Youth Peace & Language Association), a nonprofit focused on English language learning for people in the Middle East, with multiple departments offering internships and volunteer opportunities. Her passion for languages, particularly Arabic, inspired the initiative, which also explores the impact of globalization and combines language learning with cultural understanding and leadership development.

TSD MISSION MOMENT - SSAB EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE MLK DAY OF SERVICE. The Board recognized the Superintendent Student Advisory Board Executive Committee, which leads the 56-member SSAB meetings by planning, setting agendas, running meetings, and orchestrating activities and events. The minutes note this is the second year the group has had an executive board, refer to "these eight students" and later to "these six individuals," and record that the committee organized and executed the MLK Citywide Celebration and Day of Service, which hundreds of families attended; photos were shared on the district Facebook page and were to appear in the Friday newsletter. The executive board members called forward for recognition and a token of appreciation were Nurayda Albeez, Elyse Lazrado, Maaz Ali, Vihaan Gehlaut, Angelina Matti, and Reah Pawar.

STUDENT SPOTLIGHT. The Board recognized creative achievement in the TSD Creative Guild, welcoming Student Board Representative from IA-East Nurayda Albeez; Mr. Thomas Butcher, Creative Guild advisor, was invited up to speak about her accomplishments.

ADDITIONS & DELETIONS: None. PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (AGENDA ITEMS): None.

GENERAL - CONSENT AGENDA. It was moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Anne that the Troy Board of Education approve items A, B, C, D, E, and F on the consent agenda: minutes of the January 14, 2025 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the January 21, 2025 Board of Education Organizational & Regular Meeting; Treasurer's Report - December 2024; Schools Closed to Open Enrollment; Schools of Choice 105 & 105c; and Secondary Course Description Book Adoption. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

PERSONNEL: None. CURRICULUM: None.

BUSINESS - ATHLETICS PHASE 2. It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mrs. Alic that the bid for the high school athletic renovations be awarded as follows and that the amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund: Cortis Bros Trucking & Excavating, Site Work, $8,315,200.00; E&L Construction Group, General Trades, 1,414,000.00; Great Lakes Hotel Supply, Food Service Equipment, 80,766.00; CSM Mechanical, Mechanical, 348,185.00; Innovated Energy Controls, Electrical, 803,307.00; Shaw Integrated & Turf Solutions, Inc., Synthetic Turf, 978,545.00; Contingency (8%), $955,200.00; TOTAL, $12,895,203.00. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

BUSINESS - MOVING SERVICES. It was moved by Dr. Melton and supported by Mr. Haupt that the bid for professional moving services be awarded to Premier Relocations, LLC in the amount of $246,180.00 and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

BUSINESS - NETWORK AND WIRELESS PROJECT. It was moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Anne that the purchase and implementation of a network and wireless solution from Cisco Networks be awarded to People Driven Technology in the amount of $2,154,355.01 and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Board members inquired about E-rate funding; Mr. Trudel said the district would be eligible for E-rate funding after April 1st. The minutes as extracted do not print a vote tally for this item.

BUSINESS - EPIC PA, BELL, AND SECURITY SYSTEM. It was moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Haupt that the purchase of the EPIC System be awarded to VSC, Inc. in the amount of $1,826,553.30 and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

BUSINESS - MARTELL CAFETERIA TABLES. It was moved by Mrs. Zendler and supported by Mrs. Anne that the purchase of cafeteria tables be awarded to School Specialty in the amount of $39,786.15 and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (NON-AGENDA ITEMS). Dr. Philippart provided the opportunity for community members to address the Board on non-agenda items. Four community members addressed the Board during public communication. No action was taken by the Board.

OTHER - IDEA FULL FUNDING ACT RESOLUTION. Background recorded in the minutes: the K-12 Alliance of Michigan held a press conference to launch efforts both to celebrate the success of the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) on the 50th anniversary of its passage and to press the federal government to fund it adequately; Congress has never funded the program higher than 18%, and this year funding has dropped all the way back to 10.3%, costing Michigan roughly $650 million this year alone. School boards in Michigan were asked to pass a resolution in support of the IDEA Full Funding Act, with signed resolutions to be shared with members of Congress at the K-12 Alliance symposium in April. It was moved by Dr. Melton and supported by Mrs. Alic. The whereas clauses state that public education is the cornerstone of democracy; that in the decade following the Great Recession students across the U.S. lost nearly $600 billion from the states' disinvestment in their public schools; that prior to the COVID-19 pandemic both state and federal funding for public schools was already failing to meet critical student needs; that since the pandemic students have needed additional academic, social, emotional, and mental health supports through targeted programming, additional personnel, enhanced professional development, new technology, and critical facility updates; that research consistently shows increased education funding positively affects academic performance, increases graduation rates, and future earnings; that when IDEA was passed in 1975 the federal government committed to pay 40 percent of the average per pupil expenditure for special education; that the financial pledge has never been met and is currently funded at approximately 10.7 percent, leaving a gap of billions of dollars; that Troy School District serves a student population that includes 10.69 percent of students with disabilities; that unfunded IDEA costs require the district to reallocate money from other programs; and that federal underfunding has negatively impacted the academic opportunities of all students for generations. The resolution calls on Congress to immediately pass the IDEA Full Funding Act (S.2217/H.R. 4519), which would create a 10-year mandatory path to fully fund IDEA, and calls on the state legislature to provide adequate, equitable, and sustainable funding increases to districts. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

OTHER - MASB BOARD OF DIRECTORS' ELECTION, REGION 8. It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Troy Board of Education cast its ballot for the following candidate to serve on the 2025 Michigan Association of School Boards' Board of Directors: Randel Meisner, Region 8, three-year term. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

REPORTS FROM HIGH SCHOOL STUDENT REPRESENTATIVES. Kristian Vitanovich, student representative for Troy College and Career High School, shared a report on events and activities at his school. Nurayda Albeez, student representative for International Academy-East, shared a report on events and activities at her school. Adam McManus, student representative for Troy High School, was not in attendance. Diana D'Aloisio, student representative for Athens High School, shared a report on events and activities at her school.

BOARD MEMBER COMMENTS/ANNOUNCEMENTS. Topics listed: Ramadan; NSBA Advocacy Institute; Career & Technical Education Month; TSD Inclusive Newsletter; Oakland County Grant Program; THS Activist Week & AHS Charity Week; TCCHS College & Career Fair; Schools of Choice addition of 70 students; AARC meetings on 3/6 Baker, 3/10 Boulan, 3/11 Smith, and 3/20 Larson; CAP Match Day; March is Reading Month; and Orchestra Teacher of the Year Wendy Stuart. Dr. Philippart announced that the next Board Workshop will be held Tuesday, March 4th at 6:00 pm at the Administration Building, the Board Winter Retreat Saturday, March 8th at 8:30 am in the Administration Building, and the March 18th Board Meeting at 7:00 pm in the Services Building.

ADJOURNMENT. The meeting adjourned at 8:55 p.m.
